input: Apply for a community allotment plot this season

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether the user wants to apply to one specific site or research and apply to multiple sites changes how much groundwork needs to be done before submitting an application.
The user's location and local authority determine which allotment body or council they apply to, the rules involved, and whether a waiting list is likely.
If the season deadline is weeks away versus months away, the urgency of each step changes significantly.
Whether the plot is for the user alone, a family, or a shared group affects the plot size they should apply for and any joint-applicant requirements.
Knowing what the user has already done (e.g., found a site, started an application) avoids re-covering ground and sets the immediate next action.
Annual plot rental fees and any upfront costs vary widely; knowing the user's budget tolerance affects which sites or plot sizes to prioritise.
The user may consider success as simply submitting an application, getting on a waiting list, or actually receiving a plot — this shapes how far the plan needs to go.

gold.taskTitle: Apply for a community allotment plot this season
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to successfully apply for and secure a community allotment plot within the current growing season.

questions.title: Are you applying to one specific site or several?
questions.description: Determine whether the user has a single allotment site in mind or wants to cast a wider net across multiple sites to improve their chances.

questions.title: Which town, city, or local council area are you in?
questions.description: Identify the user's location so the plan can reflect the correct allotment authority, application portal, and local waiting-list reality.

questions.title: When does this season's application window close?
questions.description: Establish the hard deadline or expected timeline so tasks can be sequenced with the right level of urgency.

questions.title: Who will be using the plot — just you, or others too?
questions.description: Clarify whether this is a solo, family, or group application, which affects the recommended plot size and any co-applicant paperwork.

questions.title: What have you already done toward this application?
questions.description: Find out the user's current progress — whether they have identified a site, registered interest, or not yet started — to set the correct starting point for the plan.

questions.title: What is your rough budget for annual plot rental fees?
questions.description: Understand the user's financial comfort zone so the plan can filter sites or plot sizes that fit within their means.

questions.title: What would a successful outcome look like to you?
questions.description: Distinguish whether the user's goal is to submit the application, get on a waiting list, or actually have keys to a plot this season, so the plan has the right endpoint.
